Here, we describe the results of a validation and replication study of the Chinese GWAS in Brazilians, using a
stepwise strategy that involved two family-based and three
independent case–control samples, resulting in 3,614 individuals enrolled.

targets.title: Genomewide association study of leprosy
targets.evidence_quote:
Here we investigated whether non-HLA genes originally
described in the Chinese GWAS are associated with leprosy
among Brazilians. Our stepwise design involving five population samples from different Brazilian regions resulted in
positive association between leprosy and two genetic markers located at the NOD2 and CCDC122-LACC1 loci.
targets.outcome_quote:
Finally, we cannot exclude the possibility that genes not
validated/replicated for leprosy per se susceptibility are
actually controlling susceptibility to endophenotype of the
disease, such as clinical forms and the occurrence of reversal reactions.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The Chinese GWAS is the explicitly retested original. NOD2 and CCDC122-LACC1 associations are confirmed, while other candidate genes were not validated/replicated. Prior replication articles are background rather than targets.

reasoning: New Brazilian samples test non-HLA associations from the Chinese GWAS; partial support across its gene findings. Article pages 1525–1532 isolated from a thesis compilation and title, DOI and author list verified.
